problem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola ${x}^{2}=-2y?$

feedback.problem: What are the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola $(x-1)^{2}=2(y-4)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The standard equation of an upward- or downward-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ is

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k),
$$

where $p$ is constant.

We can rewrite the given equation as

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =4(\frac{1}{2})(y-4).\end{aligned}
$$

It is now clear that our equation is of the standard type with $p=\frac{1}{2}.$

Comparing our equation with the standard equation, we can see that we have $h=1$ and $k=4.$ Therefore, the coordinates of the vertex of the parabola are $(1,4).$
